figures.finding: From the 2026-27 tax year (1 July 2026) a resident pays nothing on the first P48,000 of taxable income, then 5%, 12.5%, 18.75%, 25% and, above P400,000, 27.5%; there is no local income tax.

figures.finding: Botswana has no social security taxes or contributions on pay.

sources.said: Social security contributions There are no social security taxes or contributions in Botswana.
The only deduction allowable from gross income is on contribution made by the employee to an approved superannuation fund.

figures.finding: Employers withhold PAYE from employment income using the BURS tax tables (daily, weekly, monthly, annual), unless the Commissioner General issues a directive; non-resident employees have their own table starting at 5% of every pula.

sources.said: An employer shall use these tables for determining the tax to be withheld from any payment of employment income unless he or she has a Directive(Form ITW 5) from the Commissioner General or written authority from the Commissioner General to use another method.

figures.finding: A non-resident entertainer (or group, or whoever receives the fee for them) bears non-resident tax of 10% on the gross entertainment fee for a performance in Botswana, discharged once withheld.
figures.applies: Non-resident entertainers, from 1 July 2026 (Income Tax Act, 2026, s. 10 and Schedule 1 para. 6(f)); final under s. 140 where withheld under s. 132(1).

sources.said: 10. (1) A non-resident tax is imposed at a rate specified in Schedule 1 on a non-resident — (a) who has derived interest, a dividend, royalty, technical fee, natural resource amount, director’s fee, or insurance premium, that is Botswana source income; (b) who is an entertainer, or a group of non-resident entertainers,who have derived an entertainment fee from the participation by the entertainer or group, in a performance taking place in Botswana; … (6) The tax payable under subsection (1) (a) or (b) is discharged, if the amount of the tax has been withheld from the payment of the income in accordance with section 132.

figures.finding: VAT is 14%; a person must register once taxable supplies in a 12-month period exceed P1,000,000 (Value Added Tax Act, 2026).

sources.said: (2) The rate of VAT shall be, for — (a) a taxable supply that is a zero-rated supply, zero per cent; and (b) any other taxable supply, a taxable import, or a reverse charged supply, a rate of 14 per cent. … 2. For purposes of section 12 (2), the amount is P1 000 000.

figures.finding: The tax year runs from 1 July to 30 June, and an individual's return is lodged within three months after it ends (by 30 September).

sources.said: “tax year” means a period of 12 months beginning on 1st July and ending on 30th June;

123. (1) A taxpayer liable for income tax shall lodge an income tax return for each tax year – (a) in the case of a company, within four months after the end of the accounting period; or (b) in the case of any other person, within three months after the end of the tax year.

figures.finding: The Income Tax Act, 2026 gives authors no special treatment: a royalty (any payment for the use of a copyright in a literary or artistic work, films and broadcast tapes among them) is ordinary income of a resident, with no resident withholding on it, and bears 15% non-resident tax when paid abroad.
figures.applies: Resident and non-resident authors, from 1 July 2026.
